subject: UNSTRING statement
notes: Rule: "The data item referenced by identifier-4 is the receiving operand for data. The data item referenced by identifier-5 is the receiving operand for delimiters." (cite.py --check 14.9.48.3 OK). Code: BindUnstring resolves identifier-4 (drefs[0]) and identifier-5 (DELIMITER IN) through host.Expr.ResolveReceiving — the receiving chokepoint — and binds each store as a MOVE into it (ImplicitMovePhrase.UnstringInto / UnstringDelimiterIn). Probes: a constant-name as DELIMITER IN (u9const.cob) -> COBOL1548 (§13.10.4 GR1); a function-identifier as INTO (u9func.cob) and a literal as INTO (u9lit.cob) are refused at parse; DELIMITER IN receives the matched delimiter (ufmtrev.cob B=[,   ]). No spec-derived test pins the receiving designation for UNSTRING INTO/DELIMITER IN specifically (pb429_page_counter_receiving covers identifier-7, a different operand), so test-ref is empty.
